title: What is a simple rule to multiply by five in the base five system?
description: A landmark times five is the next landmark, so the distributive property turns multiplying by five into a change of every symbol. The rule is checked on the number one hundred forty three from the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: in base five, multiplying by five moves every symbol up one landmark, because each part is multiplied by five. Watch for students who move only the biggest symbol.

source: Figure it Out (bases and their limits, question 3)
video_script.why: The child uses the multiply-by-ten rule of the Egyptian example to find the matching rule for five in the base five system.
video_script.substitution: The base is five, so each landmark times five is the next landmark.
video_script.anchor: the book's base five shapes and its number one hundred forty three, written with a circle, three squares and three triangles
video_script.payoff_line: To multiply by five, replace every symbol by the symbol of the next landmark.

final_answer.value: Replace every symbol by the symbol of the next landmark
final_answer.spoken: to multiply by five, replace every symbol by the symbol of the next landmark

hold_back: Replace every symbol by the symbol of the next landmark
maths_rules: 1 x 5 = 5; 5 x 5 = 25; 25 x 5 = 125; 125 x 5 = 625: each landmark times 5 is the next landmark
distributive property: (a + b + c) x 5 = a x 5 + b x 5 + c x 5, so multiply every symbol by 5
so each triangle becomes a square, each square a hexagon, each hexagon a circle, each circle a wave
check: 143 = 125 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 1 circle, 3 squares, 3 triangles; times 5 gives 1 wave, 3 hexagons, 3 squares = 625 + 75 + 15 = 715; and 143 x 5 = 715
video_script.design: One idea: every symbol moves up one landmark. The row of shapes stays on the board, with an arrow from each shape to the next.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the base five shapes.
<bookmark mark='sym'/>A triangle is one, and a square is five. <bookmark mark='sym2'/>A hexagon is twenty five, and a circle is one hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must give a simple rule to multiply any number by five. What happens to the shapes?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board with the empty box

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the line (a + b + c) x n = an + bn + cn; the Egyptian rule: multiplying by ten moves each symbol up one landmark

marks.egypt: the Egyptian rule for ten appears with arrows up the row

narration: <bookmark mark='dist'/>A sum times a number is each part times that number, added.
<bookmark mark='egypt'/>In the Egyptian system, we used this to multiply by ten. We will do the same here with five.

marks.given: the base five shapes and the multiplier 5 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the base five shapes, and the number five to multiply by.

beats.on_screen: To find: a simple rule to multiply by 5

marks.find: the words a simple rule are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find a simple rule to multiply any number by five.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, multiply each landmark by five. One times five is five.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five times five is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='land'/>Twenty five times five is one hundred twenty five, and that times five is six hundred twenty five. Each answer is the next landmark.

beats.on_screen: triangle x 5 = square; square x 5 = hexagon; hexagon x 5 = circle; circle x 5 = wave

marks.arrows: an arrow runs from each shape to the next shape in the row

narration: <bookmark mark='arrows'/>Step two, name the shapes. A triangle times five is a square, and a square times five is a hexagon. A hexagon times five is a circle.

beats.on_screen: any number = a sum of shapes; multiply every shape by 5 (distributive property); each shape moves up one landmark

marks.split: a number is split into its shapes
marks.up: every shape moves up one landmark

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step three, take any number as a sum of its shapes. By the distributive property, we multiply every shape by five.
<bookmark mark='up'/>Each shape moves up to the next shape in the row. The number of each stays the same.

beats.on_screen: check: 143 = 1 circle, 3 squares, 3 triangles; x 5 gives 1 wave, 3 hexagons, 3 squares = 625 + 75 + 15 = 715; 143 x 5 = 715

marks.num: 143 is written as 1 circle, 3 squares and 3 triangles
marks.move: each shape moves up to give 1 wave, 3 hexagons and 3 squares

narration: <bookmark mark='num'/>Step four, check with one hundred forty three from your book. It is one circle, three squares and three triangles.
<bookmark mark='move'/>Moving each shape up gives one wave, three hexagons and three squares.

<bookmark mark='check'/>Their values are six hundred twenty five, seventy five and fifteen, which add to seven hundred fifteen. <bookmark mark='check2'/>And one hundred forty three times five is also seven hundred fifteen.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Replace every symbol by the symbol of the next landmark
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>To multiply by five, replace every symbol by the symbol of the next landmark.
